title: fix(plugin-gantt): clear the error when the current reload commits rows (objectui#10578)
body:
Fixes #10578

Clause-②: no

The gantt recovers from a failed load on the next successful one; no export, schema or accept set moves.

## What changed

`ObjectGantt`'s `reload()` set `error` in one place: the fetch `catch`, on a non-silent failure of the current reload. It cleared it nowhere, and the render returns the error screen early on `if (error)`. So after one failed load, every later load that succeeded still wrote `data`, but the chart stayed on the error screen until a remount.

Now the **current** reload clears `error` when it **commits rows**. That happens on both commit branches (the host `data` array and the adapter `find`), silent or not, inside the existing `isCurrent()` guard. A superseded run's answer is discarded, and its clear is discarded with it.

Files: `packages/plugin-gantt/src/ObjectGantt.tsx` (the fetch callback's `error` state only), `packages/plugin-gantt/src/ObjectGantt.errorClears-10578.test.tsx` (new, 7 cases), `.changeset/10578-gantt-error-clears.md` (`'@object-ui/plugin-gantt': patch`).

## Start or success: success, and why (objectui#7237)

`ObjectGrid` clears its error when a load starts (`setError(null)` beside `setLoading(true)` in its load effect). The gantt deliberately does not:

- A start clear is safe only if the run that cleared also reports its own failure. `ObjectGrid` has no silent mode, so every grid load that clears also reports. The gantt does have one: since objectui#7237, a silent reload's failure keeps the last good rows and never sets the error.
- **Measured** (the committed pin "why the error is not cleared when a reload STARTS", plus a probe that was not committed): there is an error on screen; the query changes (a non-silent reload, in flight); a data invalidation starts a silent re-read that overtakes it; both fail. On base, an error stays up. With a start clear (ablation A3, `ObjectGrid`'s precedent), the first query's rows come back with no error and no refreshing state. That is the state objectui#7237 rules out: "the rows on screen answer the previous query, and once the refreshing state clears nothing would tell the user that".
- So the error stays until rows that answer the current query land. Before the first paint, the loading placeholder still shows while a query is in flight (`loading` is checked before `error` in the render; pinned). After the first paint, a changed query's in-flight state sits behind the error screen, exactly as on base. The objectui#10539 refreshing state is not newly hidden: base draws it behind the same early return.
- **Silent success after an error clears it.** A silent reload re-reads the current query, so the rows it commits answer that query. This matches how `ObjectGrid`'s re-read ends: the error is cleared and the rows land. **Silent failure after an error** leaves the error up.

## Pins: red on base, green on head

Base `adeecd666`, with `ObjectGantt.tsx` swapped to the base blob and the new pin file run against it: `Tests 3 failed | 4 passed (7)`. Head `49ba9b84e`: `Tests 7 passed (7)`.

| Pin | base | head | ablation that turns it red |
|---|---|---|---|
| fail, then succeed, BEFORE the first paint: the chart renders | RED | green | A4, A5 |
| fail, then succeed, AFTER the first paint: the chart renders | RED | green | A4, A5 |
| a SILENT reload that succeeds after an error clears it | RED | green | A4, A5 |
| control: fail, then fail again, the newer failure is shown | green (base never clears) | green | A5 |
| a SUPERSEDED reload that succeeds does not clear the current error | green (base never clears) | green | A1 |
| control: a SILENT reload that fails after an error leaves it up | green (base never clears) | green | A2, A5 |
| why the error is not cleared when a reload STARTS (overtaking) | green (base never clears) | green | A2, A3, A5 |

Four of the seven cannot fail on base, because base clears nothing. Their red leg is the ablation named beside them, run on the committed head.

## Ablations

Each leg went through `ablation-replace.mjs` in WRAP mode (the anchor must hit, and the landing is proven by an anchor count of 1 to 0 and a blob change), ran the pin file, and restored from `HEAD`. The restore was proven by blob equals HEAD (`31b21cc232b0`) and an empty `git diff HEAD`.

- A1, the success clear moved outside `isCurrent()`: 1 failed (superseded).
- A2, a start clear on every run: 2 failed (silent-fail control, overtaking).
- A3, a start clear on non-silent runs only (`ObjectGrid`'s shape): 1 failed (overtaking).
- A4, the adapter commit's clear removed: 3 failed (the three success pins).
- A5, a clear in the current run's `finally`: 7 failed.

A2 and A3 were no-ops on the first attempt. The replacement text contained the anchor, so the tool refused on its own disk check (anchor count 1 to 1) and no test ran. Both were re-run with an anchor spanning the insertion point, and the results above are from that re-run.

## Local verification (HEAD `49ba9b84e`)

- The dependency closure was built first: `turbo run build --filter='@object-ui/plugin-gantt^...' --concurrency=2` gave `Tasks: 12 successful, 12 total`.
- `pnpm exec vitest run packages/plugin-gantt/`: `Test Files 78 passed (78)`, `Tests 595 passed (595)`.
- `pnpm --filter @object-ui/plugin-gantt type-check`: exit 0, and the script name is echoed. The new test file is in the `tsconfig.test.json` program (`--listFilesOnly`: 1 hit).
- Gates, each exit 0:
  - `check-changeset-presence`: "2 source file(s) of 1 released package(s) changed, and this change declares 1 changeset(s)".
  - `check-changeset-no-major`, `check-changeset-overwrite`, `check:pending-changeset-literals`.
  - `check:new-line-citations`: "VERDICT new-cross-file-line-citations: 0 new citation(s)".
  - `check:control-bytes`: OK.
  - `check:vi-mock-specifiers`, `check:vi-mock-inherit`, `check:vi-mock-override-shape`, `check:test-path-roots`, `check:shell-escape-residue`: OK.
  - `check-changeset-claims` (report-only): details under Acceptance notes.
  - `check-governed-queue-guard --test` over the three paths: NOT GOVERNED.
- Lint was narrowed to the two touched source files. The eslint config lints `**/*.{ts,tsx}` with `tseslint.configs.recommended` and no `parserOptions.project`, so no type-aware rule exists and this diff cannot move any untouched file's verdict. The `--format json` output counted 2 files: 0 errors on both. `ObjectGantt.tsx` has 84 warnings on base and 84 on head. The new test file has 7 `no-explicit-any` warnings, the same `any` pattern the sibling objectui#7237 pins use. There is no `--max-warnings`.
- Doc and readme gates: none are reached. The diff touches no doc, README or export.

## Acceptance notes

- The error screen's English literal `Error: {error.message}` is adjacent to this change and untouched, per the claim. objectui#10578 is scoped to the clear only.
- **Pre-existing, reported to the seat and not changed here:** a silent re-read that overtakes an in-flight changed query and then fails leaves the chart on the previous query's rows. No error and no refreshing state are shown, and the changed query's own answer is discarded (it is non-current), even when it succeeded. The probe read this identically on base `adeecd666` and head: the first query's rows are shown, no error, no refreshing. The silent run re-read the changed query (`$orderby` desc for both the changed query and the silent re-read), so the rows on screen answer neither query the user asked for last. This PR's only interaction is the one pinned above: it does not widen that path.
- `check-changeset-claims` lists two pending changesets that name `ObjectGantt.tsx` (`6475-gantt-block-face-declared.md`, `6939-objectql-record-source-refinement.md`). Both describe `getGanttConfig` and the record-source ladder, which this diff does not touch, so both are still true.
- Branch history: the first commit (`226f56c35`) cleared at the start of non-silent reloads, as `ObjectGrid` does. The probe above showed why that is wrong for the gantt, and `49ba9b84e` replaced it within this PR. The squash lands only the final state.
